mechanism_book_wording: classic pathways of hormone gene transcription through their cognate receptors, as well as "non-genomic" actions
quote: Oestradiol and progesterone receptors (ERs and PRs respectively) belong to the large family of nuclear receptors (NRs), sharing several structural features
numbers_given: relative potency, dose, bioavailability, metabolite ratio
numbers_detail: PDF 326: 'a potency of approximately ten times that of estrone'. PDF 332 (Table 1): 'Micronized 17 beta oestradiol 1, 2 mg'; 'Oestradiol valerate 1, 2 mg'; '17 beta oestradiol (patch) 25, 37.5, 50, 75, 100 μg/day'; 'Oestradiol (gel) 1 mg/ 1g'; 'Oestradiol (implant) 20, 50, 100 mg'; 'Estradiol (tabs) 25μg'. PDF 336: '(~ 1,5 mg/day) compared to parenteral routes (patch ~ 50μg/24h)'; oestrone/oestradiol ratio 'approximately 5:1' after oral and 'approximately 1:1' after transdermal administration. PDF 337: 'a very low bioavailability [0.1 – 12%] of oral micronized 17β-oestradiol'.
notes: The book does not use the word 'agonist' for oestradiol. Direction (Agonist) is inferred from PDF 328: receptors are inactive prior to ligand binding and, in the presence of their ligands, bind hormone-response elements and modulate target gene expression. The chapter also uses the spellings estradiol, 17β-estradiol and 17β-oestradiol. No receptor affinity values are given.
